A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACoT-VLA and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Retained material can be matched reliably across pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation benchmarks, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and real-world robot experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds training variants, zero-shot evaluations, and Genie Sim 3.0 simulation-to-real results.

M1.justification: The EAR, IAR, action-guided prediction, flow-matching objectives, teacher-forcing procedure, and inference mechanism remain unchanged in Section 3. Additional backbone-training configurations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds Genie Sim 3.0 coverage: color-, size-, and category-based object selection and tabletop organization, with simulation-trained policies evaluated in simulation and reality. This introduces a distinct transfer scenario beyond the retained simulation benchmarks and experiments trained on real-world demonstrations.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GO-1 and VLA-Adapter to the LIBERO comparison. Table 2 removes OpenVLA-OFT+, while retaining OpenVLA-OFT. Most comparator membership remains unchanged; the new Genie Sim comparison uses the existing π0.5 baseline.

E3.justification: V2 adds LIBERO-trained zero-shot evaluation on LIBERO-Plus alongside the retained supervised setting, reports configurations with and without LLM freezing, and introduces simulation-trained real-world deployment on Genie Sim. Section 4.2 also corrects LIBERO's stated total from 500 to 2,000 rollouts while retaining 40 tasks and 50 trials per task; this does not establish additional runs.

E4.justification: The robustness analysis expands to test LIBERO-Plus generalization without training on that benchmark and simulation-to-real performance retention in Appendix C. Existing EAR/IAR, reference-horizon, KV-cache, model-scaling, denoising, and latency analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Per-task repetition practices remain unchanged, and the new transfer experiment introduces no uncertainty estimation. The corrected LIBERO evaluation total is a sample-count reporting change covered under E3.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add baseline and training-configuration results. V2 retains the original LIBERO mean of 98.5% and LIBERO-Plus supervised mean of 84.1%, adding zero-shot means of 83.6% and 86.6% and a non-frozen supervised result of 88.0%. New Table 11 reports Genie Sim averages of 84.2% in simulation and 82.9% in reality, versus π0.5's 75.7% and 77.5%. These are additional settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–12 retain the same mathematical content. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain action-space reasoning through complementary EAR/IAR modules and strong simulation and real-world performance. V2 removes benchmark percentages from the abstract and contribution summary, but retains the underlying claims and corresponding results elsewhere.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly attributes simulation-to-real performance retention to kinematically grounded action priors that remain invariant to visual perturbations. Section 4.2 distinguishes generalization findings by evaluation regime. The computational and action-representation limitations in Appendix D are unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, identifies frozen LLM backbones in existing result tables, and clarifies checkpoint provenance and training regimes. These annotations disclose previously unstated details rather than establishing changes to retained experiments. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and Appendix B training details remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to VLA-Adapter and Genie Sim 3.0. GO-1 uses the already-cited AgiBot World work. The related-work organization and positioning of action-space reasoning against linguistic and visual intermediaries remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 condenses benchmark descriptions and headline summaries, edits the conclusion and terminology, and adds a transfer-evaluation paragraph in Appendix C. The overall narrative, section order, and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 is reorganized into zero-shot and supervised blocks; Table 1 gains rows, and several captions gain configuration annotations. A new Genie Sim table becomes Table 11, moving the unchanged efficiency table to Table 12. Figures 1–4 retain their content, with limited layout reflow elsewhere.

improvement.justification: V1 combined zero-shot baselines and models trained on LIBERO-Plus in one comparison. V2 separates these regimes, supplies its own zero-shot results, and identifies backbone freezing, resolving a material comparability problem in the central robustness evidence. Direct simulation-to-real evaluation further strengthens generalization support. Its missing trial counts and uncertainty estimates, and the untested invariance explanation, limit that additional evidence but do not outweigh the improved evaluation validity.
